value.notes: Controlled set of pressed toggle values.

multiple.notes: false = single-press accordion behaviour (pressing one unpressed the others); true = any number pressed.

loopFocus.notes: Wrap arrow-key focus from the last item back to the first.

renderProp.mechanism: render on ToggleGroup; children are Toggle parts carrying value
renderProp.elementForm: render={<div />} or a Toolbar part (source: the render element is enabled when a toolbar context exists)

controlled.note: Value is always an ARRAY, even when multiple is false — React Aria's single-select ToggleButtonGroup hands back one value, so call sites need a rewrite here.

formIntegration.note: No form participation. Renders role="group" (no aria-orientation on the group; orientation is exposed as data-orientation).

keyboard.keys: Roving focus via internals/composite: ArrowUp/ArrowDown/ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, Home, End; loopFocus (default true) wraps at the ends; orientation is inferred from the orientation prop / data-orientation.
keyboard.focus: One tab stop for the group, arrows move within it.

notableDifferences: React Aria's ToggleButtonGroup takes value: string[] too, but selectionType="single" narrows to one value; Base UI always speaks arrays and switches behaviour with multiple.
React Aria exposes selectionMode/selectionBehavior; Base UI exposes multiple + loopFocus + orientation only.
State attributes are data-multiple / data-orientation / data-disabled — there is no data-selected.
The group is a plain div with role=group; it does not own aria-pressed — each Toggle does.
